title: Hardening spring

source.credit: Rendered by Ansatz with known physics (a hardening spring: k/m = 60 s⁻², k₃/m = 4000 m⁻²s⁻², b = 0.45 s⁻¹)

slow_motion.evidence: No on-screen text or visual effect indicates slow motion.

subjects.description: small orange rectangular block attached to the lower end of a vertical spring

observation.what_happens: An orange block hanging from a vertical spring oscillates up and down. It moves between a lower stretched-spring position and a higher compressed-spring position, and the oscillation continues for the whole clip.

calibration.note: metre stick = 1 m (given with the clip) spans 759 px in SAM's mask

given: scale: metre stick = 1 m (given with the clip) spans 759 px in SAM's mask, its length taken as exact
reasoning: The s channel shows ~0.25 m peak-to-peak near-sinusoidal vertical oscillation with period ~0.7 s that persists but with slowly shrinking peaks, suggesting a spring-mass oscillator with light air damping. Candidates go from ideal undamped textbook motion to linear viscous damping to linear plus quadratic drag to test whether energy loss is zero, proportional to speed, or stronger at high speed.

candidates.ifItWins: The oscillation amplitude does not decay, so air damping is negligible over the clip and an ideal textbook spring suffices.

caveats: Tracking looks only at motion along the spring, so sideways wobble would be missed.
The strong stiffening is measured only over the seen stretch and may not extrapolate farther.
Damping is treated as simple linear friction.
critique.finding: It bobs around a rest length of {s_eq} at rate {omega} with gentle damping {gamma}. The spring gets extra-stiff when pulled far, controlled by {beta}.
critique.headline: Orange block bounces on stiffening spring with gentle damping
critique.why_it_won: The simple spring misses how the bounce speeds up at large stretch, which the cubic stiffening captures.

headline: Muse Spark’s laws missed. Muse Wonder, with a fitting tool, found the spring stiffens.
finding: Its cubic law predicts the last 30%, which no law was fitted to, to 0.2 mm, against 4.7 cm for Muse Spark’s best, and recovers the hidden stiffening k₃/m = 4012 ± 17 m⁻²s⁻² against a true 4000, with ω₀ = 7.747 rad/s (true 7.746).

eyeball.confidence: low - visual estimate of period ~1s and slow decay over many cycles, no calibrated scale or timestamps available
eyeball.law_in_words: vertical damped harmonic motion about equilibrium: acceleration = -omega^2 times displacement from s_eq minus gamma times velocity

wonder.idea: The winner misses even the frames it was fitted to by 48.3 times the measurement noise; some effect is missing.
